about: A seller's own shop website (not a marketplace). The user presses 'Check this website' in the extension; Safely reads a few of the site's own pages plus outside records, then shows one card per check and a risk score. A check counts as one scan.
how_to_change: warning_points: how much a card adds to the score when it is a warning. Change the number, then deploy.
points_when_value: a different number for one exact card value.
enabled: false removes the card from every website check and from the score.
step: the build step that adds the card (1 is built first). Cards of later steps are not shown until their step is built.
A new card needs code once; after that its points and on/off live here.

pages_read.how: Browser first: the extension loads the shop's own pages from the same site. ScraperAPI only when a page is missing or is a robot check.

outside: WHOIS (domain age, owner hidden or not)
DNS (email set up for the domain)
Safely's own history and buyer reports

rules: Follow robots.txt. Never fill in a form, sign in, add to a cart or buy anything.
Only contact details the site itself gives count: a phone, an email or an address. A contact form alone is not a contact channel.
A Gmail or Hotmail address is a note, not proof of a scam.
A brand-new domain is a warning, not proof of a scam.
Judge the shop (the domain), not one product page.

cards.what_it_checks: The domain does not copy a famous brand's name or domain (lookalike letters, small spelling changes).
Scam reports from Safely users and earlier checks of this website.
When the domain was registered (a few weeks old is a warning).
An email on the site's own domain, and the domain set up to receive email; only Gmail or Hotmail is a note.
A real address, a phone and a registration or tax number on the site.
At least one direct channel: phone, email or address.
Shipping, returns/refund, terms and privacy pages exist and are real (not empty, not copied from another shop).
The ways to pay the site shows; only bank transfer, crypto or gift cards is a warning.
Prices that are too good to be true (for example 80% off everything).
Pressure tactics: countdown timers, 'only 2 left' on every product, 'offer ends today'.
Does this look like a real, operating shop (no made-up, impossible or self-contradicting details)?
Domain owner hidden, and a certificate issued only days ago.
Ratings and recent complaints on Trustpilot, Sitejabber, ScamAdviser, Reddit.
The site is listed as phishing or malware (Google Safe Browsing and similar lists).
The shop's social pages exist and are real; scam mentions online.
Security or 'verified' badges that are only a picture, not a real link to the badge company.
Reviews on the shop itself that look copied or fake.
Product photos found on other shops (copied photos).
When the site was first seen, and whether the domain sold something completely different before.
